b.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's front desk with two specialists.

  • AI Agent · Front desk: small model, Max Iterations 4, no tools except two AI Agent Tool sub-nodes. System message: "You route customer messages. Use orders_agent for prices, totals, delivery dates and order status. Use policy_agent for refunds, cancellations, substitutions and business accounts. Never answer policy questions yourself. Pass the customer's message on unchanged and return the specialist's answer."
  • orders_agent: description "Answers questions about prices, quotes, delivery dates and order status." Tools: get_price, calculator, check_delivery_date (4.2).
  • policy_agent: description "Answers questions about what a customer is entitled to under Harvest Lane's policies." Tool: search_policies (4.4) with the grounding rules.
MessageExpectedTrace
How much for 3 crates of tomatoes?ordersorders
Can you deliver to Jericho on Saturday?ordersorders
Where is HL-0042?ordersorders
Is delivery free on ₦35,000?ordersorders
Price of 2 bags of tatashe?ordersorders
Half my eggs were brokenpolicypolicy
Can I cancel at 8 p.m.?policypolicy
You swapped my tatashe without askingpolicypolicy
Hotel on weekly plan, when do we pay?policypolicy
Late delivery, can I get money back?policyorders (wrong)

9 of 10. Fix: add "late delivery refunds" to policy_agent's description.
mistakes: Giving the front desk its own lookup tools, so it answers directly instead of routing.
Specialist descriptions that overlap (both mention "delivery"), so routing is a coin toss.
Judging routing from the final reply instead of the execution trace.
No Max Iterations on the specialists, only on the front desk.
b.pass: Ten messages (five per specialist) with trace screenshots showing at least nine routed correctly, and no policy answer coming from the front desk itself.
b.redo: Send it back if routing is judged without traces, fewer than nine are correct, or the front desk answers any policy question on its own.

s.answer:
Worked example: a reviewer on the 4.4 policy answers.

AI Agent · Reviewer: careful model, no tools except reading the retrieved passages passed in. Structured Output Parser schema: { "approved": boolean, "issues": [string] }. Checklist:

  1. Every claim appears in the retrieved passages.
  2. Money rules are quoted exactly.
  3. A section is named, or the answer honestly says "not sure".
  4. No refund is promised.
  5. Under 80 words.

Flow: policy agent → reviewer → IF approved → send. Otherwise → policy agent once more with the issues → send, and if still not approved, send the safe fallback "I'll ask Tolu and get back to you" and alert Tolu.

Without reviewerWith reviewer
Errors in 10 cases31
Kinds of error2 paraphrased money rules, 1 unsure answer stated as fact1 paraphrase the reviewer missed
Model calls per case (average)34.6
Tokens per case (average)5,2008,900
Reply time (average)6 s11 s

The reviewer caught the two paraphrased refund rules and the "stated as fact" case; it missed one paraphrase about cancellation charges because the passage wording was close. That miss is now a new test case.

Decision: keep, because policy answers involve money and two of three errors were refund wording. Review again after a month: if the reviewer rarely rejects, replace it with a code check for quoted sentences.
mistakes: A reviewer brief like "check it's good" with no checklist.
A free-text verdict, so the IF node can't read approved reliably.
Running the "with" and "without" cases on different questions.
Leaving out cost and time, so the decision rests on errors alone.
No exit after the one allowed revision, so a rejected answer still has nowhere to go.
s.pass: A reviewer with a written checklist and a structured verdict, capped at one revision, and a log comparing the same 10 cases with and without it on errors and extra cost per case, ending in a stated keep-or-remove decision.
s.redo: Send it back if there's no cap, the verdict isn't structured, the comparison uses different cases, or the cost difference is missing.

g.answer:
Worked example: a fictional pharmacy in Ibadan wants a weekly "best supplier price" report across four distributors' price lists.

Team (orchestrator–workers):

RoleModelToolsCap
LeadMid4 worker agents as toolsMax Iterations 6
Worker ×4 (one per distributor)SmallRead that distributor's emailed price listMax Iterations 4
WriterStrongNone1 call
EditorCarefulNone1 revision round, then the owner

Hand-offs: worker → lead: { distributor, items: [{ product, pack, price, date, source }] }; lead → writer: { week, best: [{ product, distributor, price, next_best }] }; editor → writer: { approved, issues }. Code node checks every price has a source and recomputes "cheapest".

Human checkpoints: the report is a Gmail draft; the owner places orders herself.

Cost (Card 4, placeholder $3 per million tokens): team ≈ 24 calls × 6,000 tokens = 144,000 tokens ≈ $0.43 per run, about $1.73 a month. Single agent ≈ 10 calls × 8,000 = 80,000 tokens ≈ $0.24 per run.

Single-agent alternative: one agent with the four price-list tools and the same output schema, plus the same code check.

Recommendation: single agent plus code check. The four lists are small and share one format, so parallel workers add cost without new quality, and the code check (not an editor) catches the errors that matter: wrong prices. Revisit if distributors grow past ten.

Submit: the one-page design, both cost estimates with inputs shown, and the recommendation.
mistakes: Recommending the team by default without comparing it to a single agent.
Hand-offs described in words ("passes the findings") instead of schemas.
A review loop or lead agent with no cap.
A cost estimate with no inputs shown, or a provider price presented as fact.
No human checkpoint before anything leaves the system.
g.pass: A one-page design with roles, models, tools, a schema for every hand-off, a cap on every loop, a human checkpoint, a cost estimate with its inputs, and a single-agent alternative with a recommendation argued from cost and quality.
g.redo: Send it back if any hand-off lacks a schema, any loop lacks a cap, the single-agent option is missing, or the recommendation ignores cost.
